title: Class sizes and support for students with diverse learning needs
asked: Ms Elysa Chen asked what MOE's current position is on optimal class sizes, given that teachers face increasing complexity in supporting students with diverse learning needs, mental health challenges and special educational needs.
response: Mr Desmond Lee said MOE's approach to class sizes is guided by students' learning needs, with more teaching resources and smaller classes for those with greater needs. He cited Primary 1 and 2 classes of around 30, TRANSIT classes of up to 10, Learning Support pull-out classes of around eight to 10, dyslexia remediation classes of four to six, and Full Subject-Based Banding subject classes of 20 to 40. Schools may deploy two form teachers on a needs basis, and trained school counsellors and special education needs officers have grown from around 800 to 1,300 over the past decade. MOE will continue to study the effectiveness of its approach, including class sizes, and is prepared to adjust strategies where necessary.
